project_type: Python report generator: JSON data -> Jinja2 HTML -> WeasyPrint PDF, with a pixel/word/colour/verdict fidelity harness (scripts/compare.py) against original PDFs. The project has a proven SECONDARY implementation (reports/secondary/**, 16 report dirs) and a lakezone success example (top-level templates/, sars_pdf/, data/, output/). This task adds the PRIMARY level.
build_system: pip + python -m module invocation. No compiled build. WeasyPrint needs Pango (present). REQUIRED FIRST: run 'pyenv global 3.11.15' so 'python' resolves; deps already pip-installed into that pyenv (weasyprint 70, jinja2, pdfplumber, pypdfium2, pillow, pymupdf) but re-run 'pip install -r requirements.txt' if a fresh shell reports ModuleNotFoundError.
test_framework: No unit test framework. Verification = scripts/compare.py, which renders both PDFs to page images and reports per-page pixel-diff %, 1px-tolerant diff %, missing/extra words, fill colours only-in-one-side, and a machine-checkable >=96% PASS/FAIL verdict (PASS = tolerant<=4% AND 0 fill-only-either-side AND 0 words miss/extra).
build_command: pyenv global 3.11.15; then render one report: python scripts/render_and_compare.py <report-dir>  OR all: python scripts/build_all.py (currently discovers reports/secondary/**; FEAT-001 extends it to reports/primary/** too).
test_command: python scripts/build_all.py  (prints '=== build-all OK ==='); per-report: python scripts/render_and_compare.py reports/primary/<scope>/<report-dir>. Palette check: python scripts/measure_fills.py <report-dir>. Grid check: python scripts/measure_grid.py <report-dir>.
verification_instructions: For each primary report: render its data.json to a PDF, then run compare.py against its reference/original.pdf. The generated PDF MUST match the original page count EXACTLY, embed real Liberation fonts (never Noto - verify with pymupdf get_fonts), reproduce the per-report measured palette on the repeating main-grid pages (measure_fills.py shows 0 orig-only / 0 gen-only there), and reproduce the grid topology (measure_grid.py). Drive tolerant pixel-diff and word-diff toward the secondary levels; the residual glyph-edge pixel noise from metric-compatible Liberation vs proprietary Arial is an EXPECTED documented floor, not a defect (see reports/README.md Decisions/blockers and reports/secondary/INDEX.md). Confirm the lakezone example and all secondary reports still render unchanged (python scripts/build_all.py stays OK).
snapshot_or_generated_files: Per report: output/report.pdf, output/report.html, output/pages/page_NN.png, output/comparison/page_NN.png, output/comparison/README.md - all committed. Regenerate with scripts/render_and_compare.py <dir> or scripts/build_all.py. The source PDFs (reference/original.pdf per report AND the top-level primary_council_pdf/ , primary_region_pdf/ trees) and the primary_council_pdf.zip / primary_region_pdf.zip bundles are committed. Re-download the sources with: python scripts/fetch_primary_summaries.py --out <dir>.

environment_constraints: Network mode OPEN_INTERNET: the live site https://sars.ac.tz IS reachable (scripts/fetch_primary_summaries.py uses the /serve-pdf?file=summaries%2F<hash>.pdf endpoint - a plain /view-results fetch returns a PDF.js viewer page, NOT the raw PDF). pip and font work allowed. FONT DECISION (identical to secondary, do NOT change): the source PDFs embed genuine proprietary Monotype Arial/Times which cannot be redistributed in-sandbox; the repo ships metric-compatible OFL Liberation faces in fonts/ (LiberationSans-Regular/Bold, LiberationSansNarrow-Bold, LiberationSerif-Bold) registered under the exact family names 'Arial' / 'Arial Narrow' / 'Times New Roman' via inline @font-face in each report's style.css, ONE family name per @font-face, NO comma fallback list, NO shared/@import stylesheet. Each report's style.css must carry its own inline @font-face blocks pointing at ../../../../fonts/ (four levels up from reports/primary/<scope>/<report>/style.css). WeasyPrint gotcha (already handled in sars_pdf/render.py): a single shared FontConfiguration is passed to write_pdf, else @font-face is ignored and text falls back to Noto.

key_patterns: Data stored as DISPLAY STRINGS (preserve exact number formatting like '49.50','289.800','100'). Fixed column fills live in each report's CSS :root, measured PER REPORT from its own reference/original.pdf with scripts/measure_fills.py (pdfplumber page.rects). Only the COMPETENCY LEVEL cell is data-driven via sars_pdf/grading.py. render.py build_context supports these data shapes: page-centric (doc.pages[].tables[]), subject/table-centric (doc.tables[]), flat one-row (doc.rows[] + doc.overall), and section-centric (doc.sections[].rows[], honouring a single-letter row.grade). Reuse whichever shape fits each report. Each report is its OWN self-contained unit (own template.html.j2, own style.css, own data.json, own reference/original.pdf, own output/). Name report dirs by LEVEL+FUNCTION with a 'primary-' prefix, NEVER by the MWANZA/MKOA instance names (those are just the sampled instance and live only inside data.json values). Extraction MUST be coordinate-based via pymupdf words (see scripts/extract_*.py for the exact pattern: group_lines by y, assign columns by x-centre), never hand-typed. Add scripts/extract_primary_*.py per report mirroring scripts/extract_council_*.py / scripts/extract_region_*.py.
primary_grading_note: Primary STD4 grade labels are in SWAHILI: 'Daraja A (Bora Sana)' [A], 'Daraja B (...)','Daraja C (...)','Daraja D (...)','Daraja F (...)'. sars_pdf/grading.py currently only matches 'Grade ([A-F])'. Extend competency_letter() with an ADDITIONAL regex for 'Daraja\s+([A-F])' (keep the existing 'Grade' regex and the GPA-band fallback intact) so the competency-level colour (the only data-driven colour) is selected correctly for primary while secondary/lakezone behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged. Store the FULL Swahili label string as the display value in data.json (e.g. competency:'Daraja A (Bora Sana)'). The GPA-band boundaries in grading.py were derived from the secondary reference; verify they still agree with the primary rows' GPA->Daraja mapping and, if the primary originals use a different band boundary, add a per-report override in data (carry an explicit single-letter row.grade for section-centric reports, which render.py already honours) rather than changing the shared bands (which would regress secondary).

grouping_guidance: Prefer FEWER, larger reports. Many of the 27 PDFs are the SAME structure with a different filter (SERIKALI=government / BINAFSI=private / JUMLA=overall, or ALAMA=by-marks / GRADING=by-grade). Where two+ source PDFs are the SAME shape, either (a) build ONE report dir whose data-driven template renders each via the multi-source shape build_all.py already supports (data_<tag>.json + reference/original_<tag>.pdf, e.g. as region-schools-rank-subjectwise does for EDK/English), or (b) build a small number of distinct-structure report dirs and drive the filtered variants through them as separate data_<tag> sources. Do NOT create 27 near-identical dirs; consolidate by STRUCTURE. Target roughly 5-9 council report dirs and 6-9 region report dirs, named primary-<function>.
